source.edition: Elementary Topology, Michael C. Gemignani, Second Edition
source.visualReview: Full supplied pages 35–37 inspected as detailed page PNGs, and the beginning of the uniqueness proof read from page 34. No content from absent printed page 29 was reconstructed.
source.boundsConvention: sourceBounds is normalized [x,y,width,height] against the full source page. Inspected detail-image pixel rectangles include graphics and their labels, excluding caption and prose.

implementation.semantics: Shape-free immutable Substance snapshots, explicit mathematical relations, synchronous eager TSX styles, fresh assembly.
implementation.graphics: All figures are native Penrose optimized shapes and typed PathData; no raster image wrappers.
implementation.appearance: Consistent subdued orange regions, gray hatching, black mathematical labels and gray axes.

verification.publicBloomDeclarationEmit: passed with the public entry point and source JSX runtime in a focused temporary configuration; unrelated in-flight example imports excluded
verification.visualReview: All three rendered SVGs were rasterized on white backgrounds and inspected against the supplied figure pages. Figure 2.15 framing was adjusted to retain the complete blob outlines.
verification.scope: Mathematical relationships and actual SVG lowering are checked; pixel-level equivalence is not claimed.

figures.sourceContext: Proposition 6 and its proof on supplied printed pages 27–28: assume y≠y′ and both are proposed limits of the same sequence; set ρ=D(y,y′)/2. The neighborhoods are disjoint, contradicting eventual membership in both.
geometry: Two equally sized hatched open balls touch at the midpoint between y′ (lower left) and y (upper right).
A dashed center-to-center distance guide carries the label ½D(y,y′).
The source's s_1, s_2 and s_n sequence markers and dashed approach toward y′ are retained as schematic drawing data.
Default proposed coordinates y′=(-1,-0.4), y=(1,0.4), with both radii equal to half their Euclidean distance.
facts: ProposedLimitOf(sequence,y,plane) and ProposedLimitOf(sequence,y′,plane); no actual ConvergesTo assertions.
NeighborhoodAt and InSpace for each ball; DisjointNeighborhoods(left,right).
checks: The shared tangent point is excluded from both strict open neighborhoods.
Sampled points strictly inside one ball lie outside the other.
The factory rejects equal proposed limits.
Substance inspection confirms two proposed limits and zero actual convergence facts.
Actual SVG renders tangent circles, dashed separation and the schematic sequence.
limits: The proof concerns arbitrary metric spaces; its circular picture is instantiated as a Euclidean geometric realization.
The source does not specify the sequence's formula. Its finite illustrated markers and guide are style-owned schematic positions.
The contact marker shows a boundary location and is not asserted to belong to either open neighborhood.

figures.sourceContext: The supplied figure and Proposition 8 proof illustrate f(N(a,q))⊆N(f(a),ρ), with x in the source neighborhood and f(x) inside the target one. Source spaces are X,D and Y,D′. The preceding Definition 6 is on missing printed page 29 and has not been reconstructed.
geometry: Two source-shaped irregular blobs labeled X and Y, each enclosing a circular hatched neighborhood.
Original labels a, x, f(a), f(x), q and ρ are retained; no extra mapping arrow is added.
Cubic vector outlines approximate the source contours. The source and target circles have independent schematic display scales (60 and 51 pixels).
facts: Generic MetricSpace, SpacePoint, SpaceNeighborhood and MetricMap objects carry mathematical meaning without drawing coordinates.
Neighborhood centers and space ownership are explicit.
checks: Substance points have no drawing coordinates or blob data.
Source and target metrics retain D and D′.
Center mapping, space ownership, continuity and the chosen image inclusion are required before drawing.
Incomplete continuity relations and nonpositive chosen radii are rejected.
Actual SVG renders two closed cubic blobs, two circular neighborhoods and four point markers.
limits: The drawing is generic and gives no numerical function or metric. MapsNeighborhoodInto is a declared mathematical witness, not a numerical proof of continuity or its universal quantifiers.
The scan's hand contour and hatch noise are approximated by smooth vectors and consistent subdued orange shading.

figures.sourceContext: Example 15: f:R²→R, f(x,y)=x, with Euclidean domain and absolute-value target. The inverse image of N(a,ρ) is {(x,y):a−ρ<x<a+ρ}, an open subset of R².
geometry: A vertically hatched strip to the right of the y-axis, crossing the x-axis.
Source labels y, x, (a−ρ,0), (a+ρ,0) and f⁻¹(N(a,ρ)) are retained.
Boundary markers are coordinate annotations. No membership assertion is made for them.
Default a=2, ρ=1; the view clips the infinite strip to 202 pixels of visible height and adds no top or bottom boundary stroke.
facts: LineNeighborhood centered at a with radius ρ and line/center ownership relations.
VerticalOpenStrip has only center and halfWidth; it has no y bounds or height.
checks: Strict x inequality excludes a−ρ and a+ρ.
Membership is unchanged for y values from −10^100 to 10^100.
Factory rejects nonpositive radii; the style checks projection coordinate, metrics, neighborhood center and matching strip width.
Changing visible clip height from 180 to 240 leaves the same mathematical Substance object unchanged.
Actual SVG renders the finite hatch viewport, axes, boundary coordinate markers and inverse-image label.
limits: The original and reconstruction show finite visible portions of an infinite strip. The clip height belongs only to Style.
The book uses filled coordinate markers at the strip edges despite the strict inequality; these are retained as axis annotations.

missingSourceNotes: Printed page 29 is absent from the supplied scan. Its prose and Definition 6 have not been reconstructed.
